intro.headline: How Valley Water recovered nearly 780 staff hours in one quarter.
paragraphs: Don Rocha serves as Valley Water’s Assistant Officer of the Technology Innovation Unit, leading the agency’s effort to integrate forward-thinking technologies across water supply, flood protection, and environmental operations.

Don recognized that valuable staff capacity was being drained by manual document retrieval and research. Driven by a vision to empower workers with the proper tools, he spearheaded Valley Water’s partnership with Madison AI to establish a centralized knowledge ecosystem tailored to the district.

photo.alt: Valley Water, Santa Clara County, California

props.title: Valley Water’s Search for a Solution
paragraphs: Serving about 2 million residents across Santa Clara County, Valley Water’s team has roughly 1,000 employees. Over several decades, complex knowledge and data have become scattered across spreadsheets and databases, which means hours of manual research for staff.

Don and his team sought an enterprise AI framework designed to securely review Valley Water’s records. His journey with Madison AI kicked off with a District-Wide model, but the real breakthrough came when Don realized just how much data and insight the model could unlock.

Valley Water built custom models for various functions by introducing five Madison AI knowledge domains: Board & Committees, AQUA, Environmental, Anderson Dam Seismic Retrofit Project (ADSRP), and Finance. During Q2 2026, staff generated 771 total conversations across these models, driven primarily by Board & Committees, which accounted for 478 interactions.
Usage across the other specialized domains includes:
AQUA, with 129 conversations for staff references and regulatory summaries.
Environmental, with 96 conversations for the California Environmental Quality Act (CEQA) and permitting.
ADSRP, with 38 conversations for the Anderson Dam Seismic Retrofit Project.
Finance, with 30 conversations for budgets and payroll queries.

quote.text: Madison AI isn’t just modernizing how we work; it’s empowering our team to move faster and work smarter. Integrating the AI models into our daily operations ensures that we can deliver exceptional service that the Santa Clara community relies on each day.
quote.attribution: Don Rocha, Technology Innovation Assistant Officer, Valley Water

props.title: Decades of records that were hard to search
props.intro: Valley Water needed to streamline access to decades of critical records without compromising data security or overwhelming staff.

items.title: Manual Research
items.description: Years of retrofit timelines, contracts, audits and reservoir questions were difficult to search through across file systems. Staff regularly spent hours sifting through contracts and agreements to complete staff reports.

items.title: Burden on Technical Staff
items.description: Heavy administrative demands were taking engineering, environmental, governance, and finance staff away from their most critical, high-impact priorities.

props.title: Five knowledge domains tailored to Valley Water

phases.title: Identifying Operational Obstacles
phases.description: Valley Water identified key administrative bottlenecks across core divisions, targeting complex CEQA permitting research, capital project contract lookups, dam safety queries, and board agenda preparation.

phases.title: Comprehensive Model Deployment
phases.description: Madison AI implemented five workspaces tailored to Valley Water to streamline workflows across water supply, environmental, capital project, governance, finance, and administrative work.

phases.title: Data Integrity and Security
phases.description: The platform was built around Valley Water’s records, ensuring all outputs are drawn from internal files and provide source citations.

phases.title: Department-Wide Adoption
phases.description: Valley Water achieved rapid adoption, reaching 173 staff members across water-supply, environmental, capital-projects, governance, finance, and administrative teams.

phases.title: Expanding to Complex Workflows
phases.description: Valley Water expanded usage to technical workflows, including in-depth research on the Anderson Dam Seismic Retrofit Project and automated drafting of board-ready staff reports.

impact.title: Saving 779 Staff Hours
paragraphs: Valley Water and Madison AI’s partnership has transformed how staff access and apply institutional knowledge. By automating decades of data, Valley Water demonstrates that with the proper tools, water districts can use artificial intelligence to empower their experts, eliminate administrative burdens, and elevate critical water management and environmental initiatives.
